Lacaena.definition: Lacaena ae, f adj, Spartan, Lacedaemonian: virgines, Poë t. ap. C.; V.—As subst, a Spartan woman, C., V.

Lachesis.definition: Lachesis is, f , *la/xesis, one of the three Fates, O., Iu.

Laco.definition: Lacō or Lacōn ōnis, m , *la/kwn, a Laconian, Lacedaemonian, Spartan, C., H., O., N., L.: fulvus, i. e. the Spartan dog, H.

Laconicus.definition: Lacōnicus adj. , *lakwniko/s, of Laconia, Laconian, Lacedaemonian: ager, L.: purpurae, H.— As subst n. (sc. balnium), a sweating-room, sweating-bath.

Laconis.definition: Lacōnis idis, f adj., *lakwni/s, Laconian, Lacedaemonian: mater, O.

Lar.definition: Lār Laris, m plur. Larēs, um, rarely ium (L.) LAS-. I. Plur, the gods of places, protecting deities, Lares (local tutelar deities): praestites, guardian gods of the city , O.: permarini, tutelar deities of the sea , L…

Larentalia.definition: Lārentālia ium, n a festival celebrated Dec. 23d, in honor of Larentia, nurse of Romulus and Remus, O.

Lars.definition: Lārs Lārtis LAS-, the Etruscan title of the elder son (opp. Aruns), C., L.

Latialis.definition: Latiālis e, adj., of Latium, Latin, O.

Latiar.definition: Latiar āris, n the festival of Jupiter Latiaris.

Latiaris.definition: Latiāris e, adj. for Latialis, of Latium : Iuppiter.

Latinae.definition: Latīnae ārum, f Latinus (sc. feriae), the festival of the Latins, Latin holidays , Cs., C., L.

Latine.definition: Latīnē adv. Latinus, in Latin, in the Latin language : publice loqui, L.: scire, understand Latin : reddere, translate into Latin.— In good Latin, properly, elegantly : pure et Latine loqui.— In plain Latin, plainly, …

Latinitas.definition: Latīnitās ātis, f Latinus, pure Latin style, Latinity : auctor Latinitatis.—In law, the civil rights of Latins (i. e. ius Latii).

Latinus.definition: Latīnus adj. of Latium, Latin: genus, the Romans, V.: lingua (opp. Graeca): (fabulae), in Latin, T.: litterae, S.: nomen, Latin citizenship, C., S.: res, O.—As subst n.: in Latinum illa convertere, the Latin language.

Latius1.definition: Latius adj., of Latium, Latin, Roman, O.

Latonigena.definition: Lātōnigena ae, m and f Latona+GEN-, child of Latona , O.

Laverna.definition: Laverna ae, f 2 LV-, the goddess of gain, patroness of rogues and thieves : pulchra, H.

Lavinius.definition: Lāvīnius (V.) or Lānīnus (Pr.), adj., of Lavinium (a city of Latium).

Lemnias.definition: Lēmnias adis, f a Lemnian woman, O.

Lemnicola.definition: Lēmnicola ae, m Lemnos+COL-, a dweller in Lemnos : Lemnicolae stirps, son of Vulcan , O.

Lemnius.definition: Lēmnius adj., of Lemnos, Lemnian, C., O.: pater, i. e. Vulcan, V.—As subst m., Vulcan, O.

Lemuria.definition: Lemūria ōrum, n the festival of the Lemures, O.

Lenaeus.definition: Lēnaeus adj. , *lhnai=os, Lenaean, Bacchic: latices, i. e. wine, V.: pater, i. e. Bacchus, V., O.— As subst m., Bacchus, V., H.

Lentulitas.definition: Lentulitās ātis, f Lentulus, the nobility of a Lentulus, Lentulity (a word coined in jest).

Lesbius.definition: Lesbius adj. , *le/sbios, of Lesbos, Lesbian: civis, Alcaeus, H.: plectrum, Alcaic, H.: pes, the Sapphic meter, H.: vinum, H.

Lesbous.definition: Lesbōus adj., of Lesbos, Lesbian: barbiton (i. e. of Alcaeus and Sappho), H.

Lethaeus.definition: Lēthaeus adj. , *lhthai=os, of Lethe, Lethean: amnis, V.: vincula, i. e. of death, H.: somnus, profound, V.: ros, soporific, V.: sucus, O.

Lethe.definition: Lēthē ēs, f , *lh/thh, a river in the lower world, river of oblivion: aqua Lethes, O.

Libentina.definition: Libentīna (Lub-) ae, f libens, a surname of Venus as goddess of pleasure .

Liber.definition: Līber erī, m LIQV-, an Italian deity of planting and fructification (identified with the Greek Bacchus), T., C., V., H.— Wine , T., C., H.

Liberalia.definition: Līberālia ium, n a festival of Liber, C., O.

Libethris.definition: Lībēthris idis, adj. f, *leibhthri/s, of Libethrus (on Mt. Helicon): Nymphae, the Muses, V.

Libitina.definition: Libitīna ae, f the goddess of corpses (in her temple were kept the funeral apparatus and the registries of death): acerba, H.—The apparatus of funerals: pestilentia tanta erat ut Libitina vix sufficeret, i. e. the dea…

Liburnus.definition: Liburnus adj., of Liburnia (in Illyria), Pr.— As subst m.: Liburnī, the Liburnians, L., V.: Liburnus, a Liburnian slave, Iu.—As subst f., a fast vessel, Liburnian galley, brigantine, H., Cs., Ta.

Lucanus.definition: Lūcānus adj., of Lucania (a district of Lower Italy), Cs., C., H., L., Iu.

Luceres.definition: Lūceres um, m one of three tribes of free citizens in the old Roman state (see Ramnes, Tities), C., L., O., Pr.

Lucina.definition: Lūcīna ae, f lux; sc. dea, she that brings to light, goddess of childbirth , T., H., O.: Lucinam pati, pains of childbirth , V.: Lucinae labores, V. — The goddess of frightful dreams : (Hecate), Tb.

Lucrinensis.definition: Lucrinēnsis e, adj., of the Lucrine Lake: res, i. e. oysters.

Lunensis.definition: Lūnēnsis e, adj., of Luna (a city of Etruria): legati, L.

Lupercal.definition: Lupercal ālis, n Lupercus, a grotto on the Palatine Hill, sacred to the Lycean Pan , V., C., O. — The festival of the Lycean Pan , L.—Usu. plur: ad Lupercalia.

Lupercus.definition: Lupercus ī, m lupus + ARC-, protector against wolves , a title of the Lycean Pan; hence, a priest of the Lycean Pan , C., V., Iu.

Lyaeus.definition: Lyaeus ī, m , *luai=os, Lyaeus, deliverer from care, a surname of Bacchus: pater, V., H., O.— Wine, H.— As adj., of Lyaeus: latex, i. e. wine, V.

Lycium.definition: Lycīum or Lycēum ī, n , *lu/keion, a gymnasium near Athens, C., L., O.

Lycius.definition: Lycius adj., of Lycia, Lycian, V., H., O.

Lynceus.definition: Lyncēus adj. , *lu/gkeios, of Lynceus (one of the Argonauts): ensis, O.—Sharp-sighted: quis est tam lynceus, qui, etc.

labasco.definition: labāscō —, —, ere, inch. labo, to waver, yield : Labascit victus uno verbo, T.

labecula.definition: lābēcula ae, f dim. labes, a slight stain, reproach : viro labeculam aspergere.

labefacio.definition: labefaciō fēcī, factus, ere; pass. labefī ō, factus, fierī labo+facio, to cause to totter, shake, loosen, make ready to fall : dentīs mihi, T.: partem muri, Cs.: Charta a vinclis non labefacta suis, opened , O.: labef…

labefacto.definition: labefactō āvī, ātus, āre, freq. labefacio, to cause to totter, shake, overthrow : signum vectibus. —Fig., to shake, throw down, overthrow, destroy, ruin, weaken : illius dignitatem: ad iudicem causam labefactari anima…

labellum1.definition: lābellum ī, n dim. 1 labrum, a little lip : Platoni cum apes in labellis consedissent: calamo trivisse labellum, V.: extendere, pout , Iu.

labellum2.definition: labellum ī, n dim. 2 labrum, a small basin (for libations).

labes.definition: lābēs is, f 2 LAB-, a falling, sinking in, subsidence : ut multis locis labes factae sint: terrae, L.— A fall, stroke, ruin, destruction : innocentiae: prima mali, first stroke of misfortune , V. — A spot, blot, stain…

labium.definition: labium ī, n 1 LAB-, a lip : tremulus labi<*>s demissis, T.

labo.definition: labō āvī, ātus, āre 2 LAB-, to totter, be ready to fall, begin to sink, give way, be loosened : illud (signum) lababat: labat ariete crebro Ianua, V.: labant naves, roll , O.: littera labat, is unsteady , O.: tarda tr…

labor1.definition: lābor lapsus, ī (lābier, H.), dep. 2 LAB-, to glide, slide, move, slip, float, pass, flow : Per sinūs, in folds , O.: Ille inter vestīs et levia pectora lapsus Volvitur, V.: Ut rate felici pacata per aequora labar, O.…

labor2.definition: labor (old labōs, T., S., Ct.), ōris, m 3 LAB-, labor, toil, exertion : ingenium ab labore proclive ad lubidinem, T.: quanto labore partum: non intermissus remigandi, Cs.: res est magni laboris: ad incertum casum labo…

laborifer.definition: labōrifer fera, ferum, adj. 2 labor+1 FER-, labor-bearing, toil-enduring : iuvencus, O.

laboriose.definition: labōriōsē adv. with comp. and sup. laboriosus, laboriously, with fatigue : est alcui laboriose, it goes hard with , Ct.: docere laboriosius: laboriosissime accusare.

laboriosus.definition: labōriōsus adj. with comp. and sup. 2 labor, full of labor, laborious, toilsome, wearisome, difficult, troublesome : deambulatio, T.: nihil laboriosius: operum laboriosissimum, L.: fabula, hard to enact , T.— Inclined…

laboro.definition: labōrō āvī, ātus, āre 2 labor, to labor, take pains, endeavor, exert oneself, strive : ne labora, T.: sibi: frustra laboret Ausus idem, H.: in spem, O.: quid est, in quo se laborasse dicit? in durā humo, O.: in omni g…

labrum1.definition: labrum ī, n 1 LAB-, a lip : apes, in labris Platonis consedisse: discidit labrum, T.: superius, the upper lip , Cs.: (poculis) labra admovere, V.: labra incana situ, O.: Compressis labris, H.—Prov.: primis labris gust…

labrum2.definition: lābrum ī, n 3 LV-, a basin, tub, bathtub, vat : labrum si in balineo non est: aëna, V.: marmorea duo labra ante fornicem posuit, L.: spumat plenis vindemia labris, in the full vats , V.: labra Dianae, bath , O.

labrusca.definition: lābrūsca ae, f the wild vine: Silvestris, V.

labyrintheus.definition: labyrinthēus adj., labyrinthine, intricate: flexus, Ct.

labyrinthus.definition: labyrinthus ī, m , labu/rinthos, a labyrinth, building with winding passages.—Esp., that built by Daedalus, near Gnossus, in Crete, V., O., Iu.

lac.definition: lāc lactis, n milk: nutricis: lacte vesci, S.: lacte vivere, Cs.: lactis Cantare rivos, H.: lac pressum, cheese, V.: coactum, O.: Qui plus lactis quam sanguinis habet, of tender age, Iu.—A milky juice, milk (of plants…

lacer.definition: lacer era, erum, adj. 3 LAC-, mangled, lacerated, torn : corpus, L.: Deiphobum lacerum crudeliter ora, mutilated , V.: funus, mangled corpse , V.: lacerum cornu caput, i. e. deprived of a horn , O.— Rending, laceratin…

laceratio.definition: lacerātiō ōnis, f lacero, a tearing, rending, mangling, laceration, mutilation : corporum, L.— Plur: genarum.

lacerna.definition: lacerna ae, f 3 LAC-, a cloak worn over the toga, hooded shawl, lacerna, travelling-cloak, military cloak : cum nullis nec Gallicis nec lacernā: caput obscurante lacernā, H.: scissa, Iu.: nostrā facta manu, O.

lacernatus.definition: lacernātus adj. lacerna, wearing a lacerna, cloaked : amica, Iu.

lacero.definition: lacerō āvī, ātus, āre lacer, to tear to pieces, mangle, rend, mutilate, lacerate : Quin laceres quemquam nacta sis, T.: lacertum Largi: membra aliena, Iu.: tergum virgis, L.: Quid miserum laceras? V.: ferro, H.: Lacer…

lacerta.definition: lacerta ae, f a lizard: virides, H., O., Iu.— Prov.: Unius sese dominum fecisse lacertae, i. e. of the smallest home, Iu.—A sea-fish.

lacertosus.definition: lacertōsus adj. 1 lacertus, muscular, brawny, powerful : centuriones: coloni, O.

lacertus1.definition: lacertus ī, m 2 LAC-, the muscular part of the arm from the shoulder to the elbow, upper arm : subiecta lacertis Bracchia sunt, O.— An arm (esp. as brawny, muscular): nam scutum in onere non plus numerant quam lacerto…

lacertus2.definition: lacertus ī, a lizard, V.—A sea-fish, Iu.

lacesso.definition: lacessō īvī, ītus, ere lacio (obsol.), 1 LAC-, to excite, provoke, challenge, exasperate, irritate : ferro virum: virum voce, V.: me amabis et scripto aliquo lacesses, i. e. force me to write in return : si non lacess…

lacinia.definition: lacinia ae, f 3 LAC-, a lappet, flap, edge, hem : illud genus obtinent, atque id ipsum laciniā, by the hem , i. e. hardly at all .

lacrima.definition: lacrima (old, lacruma), ae, f a tear: cito exarescit lacrima: lacrimam dare ignoto, shed a tear for, O.: homini lacrimae cadunt gaudio, he sheds tears of joy, T.: lacrimis oculos suffusa nitentī s, her eyes moistened …

lacrimabilis.definition: lacrimābilis e, adj. lacrima, worthy of tears, lamentable, moving, mournful : nil lacrimabile cernit, O.: gemitus, V.

lacrimabundus.definition: lacrimābundus adj. lacrimo, bursting into tears , L.

lacrimo.definition: lacrimō (old, lacrumō), āvī, ātus, āre lacrima, to shed tears, weep : nequeo quin lacrumem, T.: Quid lacrumas? T.: lacrimans mater, in tears : oculis lacrimantibus: Multa super natā lacrimans, V.— To bewail, lament : …

lacrimosus.definition: lacrimōsus adj. lacrima, full of tears, tearful, weeping : lumina vino (i. e. oculi), O.— Causing tears, moving to tears, lamentable, doleful : fumus, H., O.: Troiae funera, H.: poëmata, H.: voces, plaintive , V.

lacrimula.definition: lacrimula ae, dim. lacrima, a little tear, tearlet : una falsa, T.: lacrimulam videre.

lactens.definition: lactēns adj. P. of * lacteo from lac, taking milk, suckling : Romulus: vitulus, O.: hostiae, L. —As subst: lactentibus rem divinam facere, L.: viscera lactentia, i. e. sucklings , O.— Yielding milk, full of milk : ube…

lacteolus.definition: lacteolus adj. lac, milk-white : puellae, Ct.

lactesco.definition: lactēscō —, —, ere, inch. * lacteo, to turn to milk : cibus matrum lactescere incipit.

lacteus.definition: lacteus adj. lac, of milk, milky, full of milk : umor, O.: ubera, V.— Milk-white, milk-colored, milky : colla, V.: circus, the Milky Way : via, O.

lacto1.definition: (lactō, —, —, āre) lac, to give milk, give suck .—Only P. praes. : Ubera lactantia, O.

lacto2.definition: lactō āvī, —, āre, freq. lacio; 1 LAC-, to allure, wheedle, flatter, dupe, cajole : animos, T.: me amantem, T.

lactuca.definition: lactūca ae, f lac, lettuce , H.

lacuna.definition: lacūna ae, f lacus, a ditch, pit, hole, pool, pond : cavae, V.: tenet ima lacunae salix, O.: caecas lustravit luce lacunas.—Fig., a gap, void, defect, want : rei familiaris: in auro.

lacunar.definition: lacūnar āris, n lacuna, a wainscoted and gilded ceiling, panel-ceiling, ceiled roof : aureum Meā in domo, H.: gladium e lacunari demitti iussit.—Prov.: spectare lacunar, i. e. be unobservant , Iu.

lacuno.definition: lacūnō —, —, āre lacuna, to panel, chequer , O.

lacunosus.definition: lacūnōsus adj. lacuna, full of hollows : nihil lacunosum, no gap .

lacus.definition: lacus ūs, m 2 LAC-, an opening, hollow, lake, pond, pool (of living water): apud ipsum lacum Est pistrilla, T.: Albanus: ad spurcos lacū s, Iu.: lacu Fluvius se condidit alto, in the water , V.: Quo te cumque lacus Fo…

laedo.definition: laedō sī, sus, ere, to hurt, wound, injure, damage: frondes laedit hiemps, O.: hominem volnere, O.: me dente, Ph.: robigine ferrum, V.: collum, i. e. hang oneself, H.—Fig., to trouble, annoy, vex, injure, insult, offe…

laena.definition: laena ae, f , xlai=na, a woollen mantle, shawl, cloak, V., C., Iu.

laesio.definition: laesiō ōnis, f laedo, a hurting, injuring, personal attack .

laetabilis.definition: laetābilis e, adj. laetor, joyful, glad, gladsome : nihil: factum, O.

laetans.definition: laetāns antis P. of laetor, joyful, glad : animus.

laetatio.definition: laetātiō ōnis, f laetor, a rejoicing, exultation, joy : diutina, Cs.

laetatus.definition: laetātus adj. P. of laetor, with joy, glad . mentem laetata retorsit, V.

laete.definition: laetē adv. with comp. laetus, joyfully, gladly, cheerfully : auctorem exstinctum laete tulit: quo faciant id laetius.

laetifico.definition: laetificō āvī, ātus, āre laetificus, to cheer, gladden, delight : sol laetificat terram: Indus agros laetificat, i. e. fertilizes .

laetificus.definition: laetificus adj. laetus+2 FAC-, gladdening, glad, joyful, joyous : vites, Enn. ap. C.

laetitia.definition: laetitia ae, f laetus, joy, exultation, rejoicing , gladness, pleasure, delight : magna laetitia nobis est, quod, etc., S.: laetitiā frui: diem in laetitiā degere, spend joyfully , T.: laetitiae dator, i. e. Bacchus ,…

laetor.definition: laetor ātus, ārī, dep. laetus, to rejoice, feel joy, be joyful, be glad : nuptiis, T.: bonis rebus: pueri fato, O.: iuvenis specie, Iu.: in omnium gemitu: de communi salute: ex perfidiā laetati, S.: etiam quod laetere…

laetus.definition: laetus adj. with comp. and sup, joyful, cheerful, glad, gay, joyous, rejoicing, happy, pleased, delighted, full of joy: Laetus est nescio quid, T.: alacres laetique: ludi laetiores: dies laetissimi: servatam ob navem,…

laeva.definition: laeva ae, f laevus, the left hand (sc. manus): petit dextrā laevāque Serestum, V.: Cognovi clipeum laevae gestamina nostrae, O.— The left side, left (sc. pars): Laevam cohors petivit, V.: laevam pete, go to the left ,…

laeve.definition: laevē adv. laevus, left-handedly, awkwardly : non laeve, cleverly , H.

laevus.definition: laevus adj. , laio/s, left, on the left side: manus: auris, O.: Pontus, to the left, O.: iter, V.: habena, H.: laevā parte, on the left, O.—As subst. n the left: fleximus in laevum cursūs, O.: In laevum conversus, Iu.…

laganum.definition: laganum ī, n a cake of flour and oil (eaten by the poor), H.

lageos.definition: lagēos ī, f , la/geios, a species of vine, V.

lagoena.definition: lagoena and lagōna (not lagēna), ae, f , la/gunos, a vessel of earthenware with rounded body, handles, and narrow neck, flask, flagon, bottle: inanes: fracta, H., Iu.

lagois.definition: lagōis idis, f , lagwi/s, a kind of bird, heathcock, grouse: peregrina, H.

lama.definition: lāma ae, f 2 LAC-, a slough, bog, fen : Viribus uteris per lamas, H.

lambo.definition: lambō —, —, ere 1 LAB-, to lick, lap, touch : hi canes, quos tribunal meum vides lambere: lagonae collum, Ph.: manūs, O.: crustula, Iu.: volnera, V.— To flow by, wash, bathe, lick, play upon : quae loca Lambit Hydaspe…

lamenta.definition: lāmenta ōrum, n 1 CAL-, a wailing, moaning, weeping, lamentation, lament : velle mortem suam lamentis vacare: lamentis lacrimisque extinctos prosequi, L.: lamenta ac lacrimas ponunt, Ta.: in lamentis luctuque iacēre: …

lamentabilis.definition: lāmentābilis e, adj. lamentor, mournful, lamentable, full of sorrow : vox: mulierum comploratio, L.: regnum, V.: tributum, deplorable , O.

lamentatio.definition: lāmentātiō ōnis, f lamentor, a wailing, moaning, weeping, lamenting, lamentation : lugubris: cotidianae lamentationes virginis: multis cum lamentationibus.

lamentor.definition: lāmentor ātus, ārī, dep. lamenta, to wail, moan, weep, lament : praetor ceteras, T.: audiebam lamentari uxorem.— To bewail, lament, bemoan : matrem mortuam, T.: vita, quam lamentari possem: ad lamentandam tanti imperi…

lamia.definition: lamia ae, f , la/mia, a witch, sorceress, vampire: lamiae vivum puerum extrahere alvo, H.

lamina.definition: lāmina or lammina or lāmna ae, f a thin slice, plate, leaf, layer, lamina: cum lamina esset inventa: tigna laminis clavisque religant, Cs.: aenea, L.: Laminae ardentes, red-hot plates (for torture): candens, H.—A blad…

lampas.definition: lampas ādis, f , lampa/s, a light, torch, flambeau: inlatae lampades, Att. ap. C.: argenteus Cupido cum lampade: Salmoneus lampada quassans, V.: coruscae, torches, O.: aenea, lamp, Iu.: praecinctae lampades auro, O.: …

lamyrus.definition: lamyrus ī, m a sea-fish (unknown), O.

lana.definition: lāna ae, f wool: quid lanae abstulerit?: lanam trahere, Iu.: lanas ducere, spin wool, O.: lanas tingere murice, dye, O.: lanam fucare veneno, V.: medicata fuco, H.: aurea, the golden fleece, O.: Tenuia lanae vellera, …

lanatus.definition: lānātus adj. lana, bearing wool, woolly : animalia, Iu.—Plur f . as subst, sheep , Iu.

lancea.definition: lancea ae, f a Spanish lance, light spear, lance, spear: lanceas portare, S.: lata, i. e. with a broad head, V.: duas lanceas dextrā praeferens, Cu.: miles lanceis adsultans, Ta.

lancino.definition: lancinō —, ātus, āre, to squander, dissipate: bona lancinata sunt, Ct.

laneus.definition: lāneus adj. lana, woollen, of wool : pallium: infula, V.: effigies, H.—Fig., soft as wool, velvety : latusculum, Ct.

languefacio.definition: languefaciō —, —, ere langueo+facio, to make faint, weary : excitatos.

languens.definition: languēns entis, adj. P. of langueo, faint, weak, feeble, inert, powerless, inactive, languid : incitare languentīs: manus, O.: vox: hyacinthus, drooping , V.: cor, heavy , Ct.

langueo.definition: langueō —, —, ēre LAG-, to be faint, be weary, be languid : nostris languentibus, Cs.: e viā, to be fatigued : per adsiduos motūs, to be wearied , O.: Inachiā minus ac me, H.: flos languet, droops , Pr.: tristi langue…

languesco.definition: languēscō guī, —, ere, inch. langueo, to become faint, grow weak, sink, be enfeebled : corpore languescit: luna languescit, is obscured , Ta.: cum flos Languescit moriens, droops , V.: Bacchus in amphorā Languescit, m…

languide.definition: languidē adv. languidus, faintly, feebly, slowly, spiritlessly .—Only comp: languidius in opere versari, Cs.: dictum languidius.

languidulus.definition: languidulus adj., somewhat feeble: somnus, of faintness, Ct.

languidus.definition: languidus adj. with comp. LAG-, faint, weak, dull, sluggish, languid : vino languidi: labore et aestu, S.: uxor, languishing , Iu.: boves Collo trahentes languido, H.: flumen, sluggish , H.: aqua, L.: aura Noti, gentl…

languor.definition: languor ōris, m LAG-, faintness, feebleness, weariness, sluggishness, languor, lassitude : me deambulatio ad languorem dedit, has fatigued , T.: corporis: languore militum periculum augetur, Cs.: ficto languore, feign…

laniatus2.definition: laniātus ūs, m lanio, a tearing in pieces, lacerating : ferarum.—Fig., anguish, remorse , Ta.

laniena.definition: lāniēna ae, f lanius, a butcher's stall , L.

lanificus.definition: lānificus adj. lana+2 FAC-, that works in wool, spinning, weaving : ars, O.: Parcae, Iu.
